# Scribl Shape Review -- 2026-09-04

Scheduled 12:00 to 13:00 CDT (17:00 to 18:00 UTC), organized by Rob Forshier
II. Invited: Matthew Kaplan and Eric Rice (Scribl), plus David Lawton, Martin
Young, John Kilgore, Angie Yap, Pramod Kumar and Pankaj Aggarwal
(Bounteous). Transcript cues run 00:00:17 to 00:44:47, so about 45 minutes.
Four people spoke: Rob Forshier II, Pankaj Aggarwal, Eric Rice, Matthew
Kaplan. Pramod Kumar, David Lawton, Martin Young, John Kilgore and Angie Yap
are on the invite but do not appear in the transcript.

This was a client-facing review, not a daily standup, run off a prepared talk
track (`artifacts/shape-review-2026-09-04.html`) in four blocks: a
20-minute walkthrough of sprint accomplishments with credit per person, a
20-minute design capture session with Eric presenting Christina's mockups
against the ratified decision register, a 10-minute sprint 1/backlog update,
and a 10-minute retro. In practice the meeting ran shorter and the blocks
compressed; block 3 (backlog) was skipped as unnecessary and folded into
Q&A.

A durable retro of the design decisions and client-facing content lives at
[`knowledge/wiki/sources/2026-09-04-shape-review.md`](../wiki/sources/2026-09-04-shape-review.md).
This page is the operational record and action-item seam.

## Summary

Rob opened by demoing the live Scribl app on his own machine at Pankaj's
request, confirming it is already front-end production-ready (mock backend
only, AWS not yet wired up). He then walked sprint 1 credits: Pramod ran
delivery and staffing, including swapping an iOS engineer out for family
leave; Pankaj laid down the engineering practice (architecture layers,
CI/CD, GitHub Actions, the ratified wiki, a `pnpm bootstrap` setup script)
and is close on the backend, pending AWS; Nitish reworked the prototype's
API contracts into production endpoints; Karuna is defining QA test
patterns to eventually bake into the team's Claude skills; Shubhankar has
been deep in iOS platform work alongside Pankaj. Rob covered his own work:
rejiggering the prototype to match the redesigned invite/onboarding flow,
building the new compose (image-composite) screen from scratch off Eric's
demo, and standing up the meta-repo's meeting-ingest automation (this ingest
being an example of it).

Eric then walked Christina's five mockup screens (main/home, login, canvas,
share, home-screen variants), with Matthew mostly listening. See the
durable retro for the full screen-by-screen decision list.

Two client asks came up mid-call: an architecture/IP snapshot for the
patent lawyers, and a capability snapshot to onboard an eventual internal
dev hire. Both are new follow-ups with no committed delivery date. Matthew
also asked about schedule position (Rob: firmer read by end of next week,
2026-09-11) and about when to bring on a fractional product owner (Rob:
probably the latter two sprints of the beta, possibly still early even
then).

The retro closed on positive process feedback from both Eric and Matthew,
with one piece of constructive feedback: Matthew felt the team was dropped
into live sticky-note workshop sessions without advance notice of the
topics, which produced groupthink. Rob committed to sending session links
earlier going forward.
